title: Signed grip-trial drift did not transfer incremental hemoglobin prediction across NHANES samples
abstract: A registered literature-motivated test asked whether first-to-third bilateral grip change predicts hemoglobin beyond flexible demographics and conventional grip summaries in adults aged60+. Models fitted to1,362 NHANES2011–2012 participants were frozen and tested in1,484 separately sampled2013–2014 participants. The pattern slightly improved source grouped cross-validation, but target weighted MSE rose from1.374177 to1.379199 (g/dL)². Baseline-minus-augmented gain was−0.005021, with joint source–target stratified PSU-bootstrap95% interval[−0.019375,0.002174]. Pain-free, maximal-effort and specification checks did not rescue the result. This is not equivalence or evidence against anemia-related muscle effects. Validation spans separate cross-sectional releases of one survey, not another measurement system.
